bindingDocumentation: Two questions, two axes. `category` answers why a canonical route exists and which part of the projection it belongs to. `binding` answers whether Rust binds it and, when it does not, why not -- with evidence, and with a durable task when the reason is temporary. A purpose is never an answer to the binding question: 'this backs XNA' says nothing about whether the Rust projection reaches it. BOUND is measured from the reviewed cna-sys slice and is never declared here; every other status must be stated, and every statement must carry a reason and evidence a reader can check.

rules.reason: these are pure value arithmetic, and cna::value implements each operation in Rust: Matrix::Invert, CreateLookAt and Decompose, Vector3::Normalize, Quaternion::Slerp, BoundingBox::Intersects, BoundingFrustum::Contains and Color::FromNonPremultiplied are Rust functions over Rust values. Binding the C route would put a second implementation of the same arithmetic behind a native call that can fail, and the two could disagree.
rules.evidence: crates/cna/src/value/, and crates/cna/src/value/tests.rs which measures the Rust arithmetic against XNA's documented results

rules.reason: cna_camera_create_with_test_backend_ext points CNA's global platform override at memory the camera handle owns, and cna_camera_destroy frees it without clearing the override, so any later camera query reads freed memory. Measured as SIGSEGV (wait status 139) from Rust; the baseline sequence without that query exits 0. Building a projection on a lifecycle that faults would mean hiding it.
